text:
Ivy L.: hey team, quick obs onboarding hiccups on day 1 — 1) Datadog: which API key should i use for quick local smoke tests vs deploying to our dev cluster? we have key rotation, so don't want to accidentally leak a long-lived key. 2) Grafana: when i open grafana i only see 'Platform Overview' and a handful of folders; our service folder (payments-api) is missing and dashboard links say 403. 3) Sentry: after SSO i can log in but Sentry shows an empty project list (no org access). who should i pester for each item and any quick workarounds? thanks!

obs-bot: Welcome Ivy! Please follow the Observability Onboarding checklist: https://go.redwood/onboard-observability and file the access form: https://go.redwood/obs-access-request — DevEx will triage in <24h.

Jordan (DevEx): welcome Ivy! quick notes: Datadog -> use a short-lived API key for ephemeral local work (we keep them in 1Password under redwood/integrations/datadog/dev/ephemeral). For k8s, use the service account-backed secret pattern; platform rotates the org key monthly. Avoid committing keys; use kubectl create secret from the 1Password value.

Jordan (DevEx): kube example:
```bash
# create secret from env var (populated from 1Password)
kubectl create secret generic dd-api-ephemeral --from-literal=api-key=$DD_EPHEMERAL_KEY -n dev-myteam
# helm values
datadog:
  apiKeyExistingSecret: dd-api-ephemeral
```
Also set DD_ENV=dev and DD_SERVICE=payments-api when running locally.

Priya (Observability): Grafana uses SSO group mappings. i just checked and payments-api dashboards live in folder "team/payments" which maps to SSO group `team:payments`. i requested SSO group add for you; sometimes you need to fully sign out of SSO and back in. if 403 persists, try the direct dashboard UID link i pasted in DM.

Kai (Platform): FYI the 403 on panels is usually the group mapping not the dashboard ACL. i've queued a re-sync for SSO groups; it can take a few minutes. if you need immediate access, i can temporarily share the dashboard as "view" for your user id.

Ivy L.: huge thanks — i saw the payments folder appear after a logout/login. Sentry still empty though  what do you need from me to get added?

Priya (Observability): sent Sentry invite to ivy.l@redwood.com and also added you to the "payments-observers" team in Sentry. check spam and the alternate inbox if your company email has routing rules. once you accept, refresh SSO and you should see the project list.

Ivy L.: got the Sentry invite, accepted, and can now see projects. two follow-ups: a) if i run local agent pointing at dev org, will traces/metrics count toward billing? b) what's our recommended sampling for local dev?

Jordan (DevEx): yes, telemetry sent to the org counts. for local dev use: set sampling low (traces: 0.01-0.05), tag DD_ENV=dev and DD_SERVICE=payments-api. For pure UI checks, run agent with no-cloud-upload flag or use a sandbox org we have for spike work.

Jordan (DevEx): local no-upload example:
```bash
# local UI-only agent to avoid ingestion
docker run --rm -e DD_API_KEY=$DD_EPHEMERAL_KEY -e DD_ENV=dev datadog/agent:latest agent run --no-cloud-upload
```
Or set tracer config: DD_TRACE_SAMPLE_RATE=0.02 for minimal spans.

Kai (Platform): we also have per-user quotas on the dev org to prevent accidental spikes, but please be mindful of high-frequency cron jobs while iterating.

Ivy L.: awesome, everything's coming together. one more ask: we rotate the org-level key monthly — any guidance on how to detect when a key is near rotation so my CI doesn't break?

Priya (Observability): good point. platform publishes key expiry in the 1Password note metadata and we push a Slack notice to #eng-infra 48hrs before rotation. for CI, prefer using the k8s secret mounted from Vault via our syncer; it handles rotation transparently. if you need help swapping a secret in a pipeline, ping me and i can walk through it.

Ivy L.: perfect, thank you all for the rapid help :raised_hands: i'll bookmark the starter dashboards and the onboarding checklist. closing out thread.

Jordan (DevEx): welcome aboard Ivy! DM us if anything else pops up. :tada:
